exposure: Grand multiparity (delivery of the fifth to ninth viable pregnancies)
outcome: Maternal obstetric complications (e.g., malpresentation, antepartum haemorrhage, preterm labour, cephalopelvic disproportion, obstructed labour, postpartum haemorrhage)
Maternal medical complications (e.g., anaemia, hypertension, diabetes)
Foetal morbidity (e.g., Apgar score < 7, low birth weight, NICU admission)
cohort: 120 grand multiparous women (delivering their fifth to ninth viable pregnancies) attending Government Lala Ded Maternity hospital Gmc Srinagar between August 2017 and March 2019.
finding: The study found high rates of maternal complications among grand multiparas, including 65% anaemia, 13.3% postpartum haemorrhage, 16.7% malpresentation, and 14.1% cephalopelvic disproportion, with 34.5% of babies having low birth weight and 35.3% requiring NICU admission.
mod_finding: The most common mode of delivery was vaginal (68.4%), followed by LSCS (26.6%) and vacuum-assisted delivery (5%).
